definitions.text: Science is a collective knowledge about the natural phenomena, processes and events occurring around us.
The biological sciences which deal with the living things.
The physical sciences which are about the study of non-living things.
Physics is the fundamental science that deals with the constituents of the universe, that is, matter, energy, space, time and their mutual relationships and interactions.
It is a study of motion and the physical effects which influence motion. It is based on Newton's laws of motion and gravitation and is often called classical mechanics.
It deal with the thermal energy possessed by the materials and it is used when it flows from one body to another.
It deals with the nature and physical aspects of audible sound energy.
It deal with the physical aspects of visible light.
It is the study of electromagnetic phenomenon and mutual relationship between electric current and magnetic field.
It explains the behaviour of particles at the atomic and subatomic level.
It explains how space and time are not absolute quantities but related to observer. It describes the relationship between them and how they are influenced by gravity and speed.
It is the study of the properties of nuclei of the atoms.
It is the study of subatomic particles and elementary particles which are basic building blocks of matter.
It is study of distribution of celestial bodies like planets, stars and galaxies.
It explores the large structure and evolution of the universe.
It is the study of some specific properties of matter in solid form.
Scientific method is a systematic approach used to search for truth of an issue and problem solving regarding natural and physical world.
Propose an explanation or a guess work known as hypothesis.
Experiment is an organized repeatable process which is used to test the truth of a hypothesis.
It is a logical explanation of the causes and effects of an issue or an event that occurs in nature.
After the careful analysis of a theory, we can make predictions about certain unknown aspects of nature.
It is a concept introduced that suggests a theory to be considered scientific if it also make predictions that can be tested and potentially proven false.

When a theory has been tested many times and generally accepted as true, it is called a law. The law is such a statement regarding the behaviour of nature which explains the observations and experiments of the past and can predict about other aspects of nature.
Technology refers to the methods and techniques developed by using scientific knowledge.
Engineering is the process of applying various technologies and scientific principles to design various instruments, tools and build things that help to meet specific needs in every walk of life.

fullMarks: For a definition or law, write the complete statement accurately; do not replace key words such as “tested many times” or “can predict” with vague wording.

For scientific method questions, give the steps in the correct order: identify the problem, observe and gather information, form a hypothesis, test it, analyse data and conclude, then repeat tests toward a law.
For a hypothesis question, state that it is a proposed explanation or guess, then give a clear example that could be tested.
For theory-versus-law answers, explain both terms and show the difference: a theory explains causes and effects; a law describes tested behaviour and can make predictions.
For Physics branches, name several branches and briefly state what each studies; do not list branch names without explaining them when the question asks you to state them.
For questions about whether theories or laws can change, finish by explaining that fresh evidence and advances in science may disprove or modify them.
For jobs using scientific knowledge, give three distinct occupations and state what each person designs or does.
mistakes: Mixing up the two groups of science. Fix: biological sciences study living things; physical sciences study non-living things.
Giving only branch names when asked to state branches briefly. Fix: add what each branch studies.
Writing the steps of scientific method out of order or skipping analysis of data. Fix: learn the numbered sequence and include recording, organising and analysing results.
Calling a hypothesis a proven fact. Fix: describe it as a proposed explanation or guess that must be tested.
Saying a law is an ultimate truth that can never change. Fix: state that theories and laws may be disproved or modified as science advances.
Claiming that a theory is rejected just because one result disagrees, without explaining the test. Fix: say that when test results do not agree, the hypothesis may be changed or rejected.
Giving examples of jobs without describing how scientific knowledge is used. Fix: say what each job designs or does, as well as naming the occupation.

shortTheory.question: Short 9.1: State in your own words, what is science? Write its two main groups.
shortTheory.answer: Science is a collective knowledge about the natural phenomena, processes and events occurring around us. The biological sciences which deal with the living things. The physical sciences which are about the study of non-living things.

shortTheory.question: Short 9.2: What is Physics all about? Name some of its branches.
shortTheory.answer: Physics is the fundamental science that deals with the constituents of the universe, that is, matter, energy, space, time and their mutual relationships and interactions. Some branches of Physics are Mechanics, Heat and thermodynamics, Acoustics, Optics, Electromagnetism, Quantum Mechanics, Relativistic Mechanics, Nuclear Physics, Particle Physics, Astronomy, Cosmology and Solid State Physics.

shortTheory.question: Short 9.4: List the main steps of scientific method.
shortTheory.answer: 1. Identify or recognize an issue or a problem. 2. Gather information through observations of its various aspects. 3. Propose an explanation or a guess work known as hypothesis. 4. Perform experiment or collect evidences to test the hypothesis. 5. Record, organize and analyze gathered data, plotting and interpreting graphs to reach at a conclusion which is called a theory. 6. Repeated tests of the theory to wide range of similar issues then lead towards the formulation of a law.

shortTheory.answer: Propose an explanation or a guess work known as hypothesis. From the above example, we assume that shadows of opaque objects are formed when they come in the path of light because light travels in a straight line.

shortTheory.question: Short 9.6: Distinguish between a theory and a law of Physics.
shortTheory.answer: It is a logical explanation of the causes and effects of an issue or an event that occurs in nature. When a theory has been tested many times and generally accepted as true, it is called a law. The law is such a statement regarding the behaviour of nature which explains the observations and experiments of the past and can predict about other aspects of nature.

shortTheory.question: CRQ 9.1: Is the theory of science an ultimate truth? Describe briefly.
shortTheory.answer: The theories or laws of Physics are man-made ideas about the way the things work. They are liable to be disproved or modified with the future advances in science which brings fresh facts and new insights about the natural and physical world.

shortTheory.question: CRQ 9.2: Do you think that the existing laws of nature may need a change in future? Describe briefly.
shortTheory.answer: The theories or laws of Physics are man-made ideas about the way the things work. They are liable to be disproved or modified with the future advances in science which brings fresh facts and new insights about the natural and physical world.

shortTheory.question: CRQ 9.3: Describe three jobs that need the use of scientific knowledge.
shortTheory.answer: A civil engineer designs a bridge that can withstand strong winds, earthquakes, intense weather conditions and heavy traffic. A software engineer designs a user friendly application of a smartphone. An aviation engineer looks for lighter material which can withstand sudden and severe disturbances and extreme weather conditions during the flight of an aeroplane.
